name: Toshiba America Foundation Grades 6–12 STEM Grants
description_short: Funding for teacher-designed, project-based STEM learning in grades 6–12.
description_full: Teachers in grades 6–12 may apply online. Grants up to $5,000 are reviewed on quarterly deadlines; requests above $5,000 use separate May and November deadlines. The foundation does not fund individuals, summer projects, clubs, or after-school programs.
eligibility_notes: Applicant must be a grades 6–12 teacher. Funding is generally directed to U.S. K–12 schools. No grants to individuals; summer, club, and after-school projects are not considered.
prize_value: Up to $5,000 on the quarterly cycle; requests above $5,000 are considered on separate May/November deadlines.

name: FIRST Team Grant Opportunities
description_short: Sponsor-funded grants for registered FIRST teams; active opportunities vary by program, location, team status, and sponsor.
description_full: FIRST maintains a live grant portal covering FIRST LEGO League, FIRST Tech Challenge, and FIRST Robotics Competition. As of August 21, 2026, sponsor grants with future deadlines are listed, including BAE Systems and Boston Scientific FRC opportunities.
eligibility_notes: Eligibility varies by sponsor, FIRST program, team status, geography, and current-season registration.

name: BAE Systems FIRST Robotics Competition Team Grant
description_short: BAE Systems sponsor grant for eligible FIRST Robotics Competition teams.
description_full: The 2026 BAE Systems FRC grant is open to teams within 75 miles of a BAE Systems site, with additional emphasis on mentor relationships and teams demonstrating diversity or economic need.
eligibility_notes: FIRST Robotics Competition teams within 75 miles of a BAE Systems site; see current application for complete requirements.

name: Boston Scientific FIRST Robotics Competition Grant
description_short: Funding intended to make FIRST Robotics Competition participation more affordable for economically disadvantaged schools and communities.
description_full: Current FIRST listing limits this grant to FRC teams within 60 miles of Boston Scientific locations in California, Indiana, Massachusetts, and Minnesota; school or community economic data is required.
eligibility_notes: FRC teams within 60 miles of eligible Boston Scientific locations in CA, IN, MA, or MN; economic-need data required.

name: Lemelson-MIT InvenTeams
description_short: Year-long invention program in which U.S. high-school teams develop technological solutions to real-world problems.
description_full: The 2025–2026 cycle awarded each selected high-school team a $7,500 grant plus year-long support. That cycle has concluded; the official page had not published a new 2026–2027 application deadline when verified.
eligibility_notes: High-school student teams work with educators and mentors; current-cycle application details must be confirmed on the official site.

name: AIAA Foundation Classroom Grants
description_short: Up to $500 for K–12 classroom projects with a clear STEM and aerospace connection.
description_full: Applicants must be K–12 classroom teachers, and grant funds are paid to the school. Current AIAA Educator Associate membership is required before receiving the grant.
eligibility_notes: K–12 classroom teacher; current AIAA Educator Associate membership required before receiving a grant; funds are paid to the school.

name: NESTA Planet Stewards 2027 Cohort
description_short: Funding for educator-led, hands-on stewardship projects addressing measurable environmental issues.
description_full: The 2027 cohort application opened June 1, 2026. Up to 10 projects may be funded, with up to $5,000 per project. Formal and informal educators working with elementary through college-age students or the public may apply.
eligibility_notes: Formal or informal educators working with elementary through college-age students or the general public.

name: October 2026 EPICS in IEEE Call for Proposals
description_short: Grant funding for student-centered engineering service-learning projects with a community partner.
description_full: Teams must include students, at least one IEEE member, meaningful engineering design, a community partner, and technology within IEEE's scope. Proposals are accepted September 1 through October 1, 2026.
eligibility_notes: At least one team member must be an IEEE member; all teams must include students and a community partner.
prize_value: Typical EPICS in IEEE awards are approximately $1,000–$10,000.

name: Delaware Education Resource Grant
description_short: Delaware grant supporting standards-based arts education partnerships and projects.
description_full: FY2028 Education Resource grants can support up to 30% of direct cash project expenses, up to $15,000. Applications open December 1 and are due March 1, 2027 at 4:30 p.m.
eligibility_notes: Eligible Delaware nonprofit arts organizations; public/charter schools and districts are eligible under the school Education Resource pathway. Review current guidelines for applicant-specific rules.
prize_value: Up to $15,000; up to 30% of direct cash project expenses.

name: Planeteer Alliance
description_short: Global youth network for climate action, training, campaigns, leadership, and access to grant opportunities.
description_full: Captain Planet Foundation describes Planeteer Alliance as a direct-to-youth program for young changemakers ages 10–25. Participants can progress through leadership levels and become eligible for campaign and leadership grant opportunities.

name: Delaware 4-H Youth Development
description_short: Statewide 4-H clubs and programs offering hands-on STEM, civic engagement, leadership, and other project experiences.
description_full: Delaware 4-H is open to youth ages 5–19 as of January 1 of the program year. There are no statewide dues or membership fees, though individual clubs and projects may have expenses.
eligibility_notes: Open to youth ages 5–19 as of January 1 of the program year. Youth may participate regardless of state residence, but competitive activities are generally tied to the state in which they are enrolled.

name: DonorsChoose Classroom Projects

name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants

name: Awesome Foundation Microgrants
description_short: Chapter-based $1,000 microgrants for locally impactful creative and community projects.
description_full: Awesome Foundation chapters independently review applications. Many chapters award $1,000, often on monthly or rolling schedules; eligibility and geographic restrictions vary by chapter, and some chapters accept applications from individuals without nonprofit status.

name: Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation Scholarship Program
description_short: The Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist children of employees who plan to continue their education in college.
description_full: The Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation has established a scholarship program to assist children of employees who plan to continue their education in college. Eligibility: Applicants to the Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation Scholarship Program must be: Dependent* children of full-time U.S. or International Trane Technologies employees who are employed with the company as of the application deadline. *Dependent children refers to natural and legally adopted children or stepchildren of the employee as well as if the employee is their legal guardian or domestic partner parent. The employee must qualify for benefits provided by the company. High school seniors/final year secondary school students or graduates, or current postsecondary undergraduates, who plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. College seniors, graduating in December of the current year, are eligible to apply to the program. Awards: If selected as a recipient, the student will receive a $2,500 USD award. Up to 60 awards will be granted. A student may receive an award a maximum of four times. Awards are not renewable, but students may reapply to the program each year they meet eligibility requirements. Awards are for undergraduate study only. Notification All applicants will be notified in May. Notifications are sent via email. When setting up your account, avoid using a school or work email. Instead, use an active, personal email address that you will continue to have access to. Please make sure to add the program email address as safe senders in your email contact list. Payment of Scholarships Scholarship America processes scholarship payments on behalf of the Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation. Payment is made in early August. Selection of Recipients Scholarship recipients are selected on the basis of: Financial need* Academic performance Demonstrated leadership and participation in school and community activities Work experience A statement of educational and career goals and objectives Unusual personal or family circumstances An online recommendation *Note: Financial need will bear the heaviest weight in evaluation of applications Applicants must complete the financial data section of the application to receive an award. Financial need as calculated by Scholarship America must be demonstrated for the student to receive an award. Selection of recipients is made by Scholarship America. In no instance does any officer or employee of Trane Technologies or the Trane Technologies Charitable Foundation play a part in the selection. Award amounts fluctuate annually based on the total number of applicants. All applicants agree to accept the decision as final. Notification Applicants will be notified in early October. College Scholarship awards are made directly to recipients from October to December through payroll. Transcripts must display: Student name School name Grades Credit hours for each course and term in which each course was taken. Eligibility: Applicants to the Ingredion Educational Foundation Scholarship Program must: Be dependent* children, age 23 and under, of active and full-time Ingredion Incorporated employees who have a minimum of one year of employment with Ingredion Incorporated and its subsidiaries as of the application deadline date. Applicants who have received a scholarship from this Program prior to the start of this current Program cycle shall not be required to meet eligibility requirements concerning any employment with the Sponsor. *Dependent children are defined as natural or legally adopted children or stepchildren living in the employee’s household or primarily supported by the employee. U.S. students Be high school seniors or graduates who plan to enroll or students who are already enrolled in a full-time undergraduate course of study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school for the entire upcoming academic year. International and Canadian students Be students in the final year of upper secondary school or upper secondary school graduates who plan to enroll or students who are already enrolled in full-time university-level studies. International applicants must be able to start university by fall 2026. (Southern Hemisphere applicants must be able to start university by early 2027.) Children of part-time employees may be eligible for the scholarship depending on local laws and regulations applicable to the part-time employee. Part-time employees should consult their local HR representative for eligibility information. Children of members of the Board of Directors or elected officers of either the Ingredion Educational Foundation or Ingredion Incorporated are ineligible. Awards: Award ranges will be determined yearly based on total fund distribution and applicant pool. Financial need will be considered when determining individual award amounts. Potential recipients who demonstrate no need, as determined by Scholarship America, may be eligible to receive the minimum award amount. Awards may be renewed for up to three additional years or until a bachelor’s degree is earned, whichever occurs first. Renewal is contingent upon satisfactory academic performance in a full-time undergraduate course of study and continuation of the program by the Ingredion Educational Foundation. Awards are granted without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sexual orientation, gender, disability or national origin. Awards are for undergraduate study only. Notification All applicants will be notified in July. Notifications are sent via email. When setting up your account, avoid using a school or work email. Instead, use an active, personal email address that you will continue to have access to. Payment of Scholarships Scholarship America processes scholarship payments on behalf of the Ingredion Educational Foundation. Payments are made in one installment. For recipients attending school within the U.S. and Canada, the individual scholarship checks are mailed in mid-August and are made payable to the college/university (U.S. Currency), but mailed to the recipient’s home address. For recipients attending university outside of the U.S. and Canada, the funds will be sent via wire transfer in September. Selection of Recipients Scholarship recipients are selected on the basis of: Academic performance Demonstrated leadership and participation in school and community activities Work experience A statement of educational and career goals and objectives Unusual personal or family circumstances An online recommendation Once scholarship recipients are selected, financial data is reviewed to determine the amount of each award. Selection of recipients is made by Scholarship America. In no instance does any officer or employee of Ingredion Incorporated or the Ingredion Educational Foundation play a part in the selection. Not all applicants to the program will be selected as recipients. All applicants agree to accept the decision as final. Application materials: As part of your application, you must upload the following: A current, complete transcript of grades. Grade reports are not accepted. Transcripts must display: Student name School name Grades Credit hours for each course and term in which each course was taken. NOTE: If you are providing SAT or ACT test scores, and those scores are not listed on your high school transcript, you will need to upload a copy of your test score report(s) separately. If you are uploading a college transcript, those scores are not required. Due to differences in educational systems, applicants from countries other than the U.S. and Canada must provide the following materials: English translations for all non-English documents. Clear photocopies of the following educational documents must be sent with the application: Students currently or previously enrolled in an institution of higher education (university) must include the following documents: Academic record (transcript of grades) for all higher education course work completed, and Upper secondary school credential/diploma/certificate. Current upper secondary school students and students who have completed less than one year of higher education (university) must include the following documents: Academic record (transcript of grades) for all upper secondary education course work completed during the past three years, and Results of academic examinations. One online recommendation form must be submitted on your behalf no later than three business days after the application deadline date. Your application is not complete unless all required materials are submitted electronically.

description_full: New York State School Facilities Association (NYSSFA) has established a scholarship program to assist children of active and affiliate members who plan to continue their education in studies leading to an associate or bachelor’s degree at any accredited postsecondary school. Eligibility: Applicants to the Fred Hack Memorial Scholarship Program must be: Children of the NYSSFA active and affiliate members who have completed one year of full-time continuous membership at the time of the application submission deadline date. Enrolled or planning to enroll in a full-time undergraduate program of studies leading to an associate or bachelor’s degree at any accredited postsecondary school for the entire upcoming academic year. Awards: Academic record Demonstrated leadership and participation in school and community activities Work experience A statement of educational and career goals and objectives Unusual personal or family circumstances An online recommendation Financial need will be considered. Preference will be given to students who demonstrate need. Notification All applicants will be notified in July. Not all applicants to the program will be selected as recipients. All applicants agree to accept the decision as final. Notifications are sent via email. When setting up your account, avoid using a school or work email. Instead, use an active, personal email address that you will continue to have access to. Please make sure to add studentsupport@scholarshipamerica.org as well as the program email address as safe senders in your email contact list. Awards If selected as a recipient, the student will receive a $2,000 award. Up to 6 awards will be granted. Awards are not renewable; however, students may reapply to the program each year they meet eligibility requirements. A recipient may not receive an award more than two times. A recipient may not receive an award two consecutive years. Awards are for undergraduate study only. Payment of Scholarships Scholarship America processes scholarship payments on behalf of New York State School Facilities Association. Payment is made in August. Application materials: As part of your application, you must upload the following: A current, complete transcript of grades. Grade reports are not accepted. Transcripts must display: Student name School name Grades Credit hours for each course and term in which each course was taken. NOTE: If you are providing SAT or ACT test scores, and those scores are not listed on your high school transcript, you will need to upload a copy of your test score report(s) separately. If you are uploading a college transcript, those scores are not required. One online recommendation form must be submitted on your behalf no later than three business days after the application deadline date. Your application is not complete unless all required materials are submitted electronically.
eligibility_notes: Applicants to the Fred Hack Memorial Scholarship Program must be: Children of the NYSSFA active and affiliate members who have completed one year of full-time continuous membership at the time of the application submission deadline date. Enrolled or planning to enroll in a full-time undergraduate program of studies leading to an associate or bachelor’s degree at any accredited postsecondary school for the entire upcoming academic year.
